action_summary: Round 25 builds and tests the only route round 24 left unmeasured: value provenance -- trace the failing run, find the expression instance that produced the value the assertion rejected, and ask whether the real fix changed that function. Only the file under repair is traced. Result: the hypothesis is DEAD as a precise localiser. 82 of 87 refused suites executed under the tracer (3 could not run, recorded); median 23 traced returns per failure; the producer of the rejected value was found in 1 of 82 (1.2%) and it was a function the fix changed in 0. Reasons, both measured: most refusals reject NO value (assert False/True and exceptions carry no operand -- 81 of 82), and when a value is rejected its producer is usually behind a public entry point in another module, which the cheap restriction to the repaired file makes invisible BY DESIGN. The result that survives is worth more than the one that died: among the 69 failures the traceback cannot localise (84%), a function the real fix changed was ON THE EXECUTED PATH in 45 (65.2%). So the observation the machine does produce for free is the PATH, not the value and not the line -- and nobody counted it before because every route asked for a line. The bottleneck is therefore named precisely for the first time: LOCALISATION BELOW THE FUNCTION. Next build, predicted before it is written: path-restricted search -- trace the run, enumerate single-token substitutions only inside the executed functions of the file under repair (the file's own tokens, dir() of the machine's types, the assertion's literals) and grade each by executing that one test; measure containment and execution cost against round 22's 4,581 baseline. Falsifiable prediction: containment in the high tens of percent, cost in the low hundreds. Four independent measurements now bound why edits are not identified by experience: word supplied 8.8%, site localised 18%, check-substitute ceiling 2.7%, value producer 1.2%. Zero model calls, zero parameters.
